label: paragraph_title
text: Chung Chau, May 4

label: text
text: In common with the surrounding areas we have been treated to a liberal supply of rain, which has delayed various building operations at Now 13, 018, 10 and 23, and has cut up some of the public which however have been attended to by the roadmen.

label: text
text:
The gardens and newly planted trees have benefitted, and the island is looking at its best. The palms must also have interfered with the attendance at the big theatre (second one has since been in progress) for which special lunches were run from Hongkong.
Dr. and Mrs. Minett left yesterday, having stayed an extra week-end to witness the school sports.

label: text
text: The athletic meeting went off very successfully; the weather conditions were ideal, as it was not too hot for the students taking part in the long list of events. The local "stadium" presented an animated scene; there was a good number of visitors present. There were several new features this year. The committee had thoughtfully provided a grandstand in the shape of a matshed shelter for the accommodation of the visitors; in case of wet weather, refreshments were also provided. Then the local mission schools attended in force and contributed several musical items. Some of the Hongkong schools had sent teams for the invitation relay race, which event was keenly contested. A likely winner had the misfortune to drop the flag so putting his team out of the running. Several of the events, notably the hopping race, had to be run again owing to a dead-head.

label: text
text: The hill race and the ung-of-war were specially interesting. The members of the committee are to be congratulated for the successful issue of their efforts.

label: text
text: We are soon to lose another of the owner-residents in the person of Mr. G. E. Wetton, who leaves shortly for England.

POLICE WORK.
H.E.'S PRAISE AT ANNUAL INSPECTION

label: text
text: Congratulations on their work during the difficult period of the strike and boycott were extended by Mr. E. the Governor to the various sections of the Hongkong Police Force yesterday on the occasion of the annual inspection.

label: text
text: The parade was under the command of the Hon. Mr. B. D. C. Wolfe, (Captain Superintendent of Police) and there were also present Mr. D. Burlingham (D. S. F.), Mr. F. H. King (Director of Criminal Intelligence Department). Inspector Blackman (Divisional Inspector of the Central Station).

label: text
text: Among the guests present work Mr. R. C. Tredwell (American Consultant-General), Mr. R. E., Lindseil Mr. H. Bloxham, Mr. E. Ralph and Mr. J. Ralston.

label: text
text:
On the arrival of His Excellency the Governor, who was accompanied by Capt. Swinton A.D.C., the parade presented arms and the Royal Salute was sounded by the buglers.
The Governor then inspected the Force after which the awards (a complete list of which has already appeared in the "China Mail"). were presented.

label: paragraph_title
text: The Governor's Speech

label: text
text: Addressing the gathering His excellence said:

label: text
text: Officers' N.C.Os. and men of the Hongkong Polka Force.

label: text
text:
Hongkong Police Force.
It am glad to have this opportunity of seeing you on parade and of congratulating you on your fine record during the critical period of the strike and boycott. In a despatch to me dated December 30th last the Secretary of State for the Colonies writes:—“I have to express my satisfaction at learning of the loyalty displayed by the Chinese members of the force and my appreciation of the work of the Police in this trying crisis.” This tribute is well deserved. Out of 533 Cantonese police, only seven deserted. Of 353 Wei-hai-well men only three deserted. Out of 105 Chinese clerks, telephone operators and sergeant interpreters, only seven deserted. Of 233 Chinese Water Police ratings, only nine seamen and five stokers deserted. Not a single coxswain or engineer left his post. This is all the more creditable because a large number of the Water Police are members of the Seamen's Union.

label: text
text: From the middle of June to the middle of August the European Police were on eight hours duty instead of six. No leave could be granted and all ranks had to be confined to their own districts. This was also the ease with the Indian and Chinese Contingents. No complaints of any kind were made and all ranks worked most cheerfully.

label: text
text: Remarkable work was done by the Police Casual Labour Department. From June 22 to July, 26 about 25,000 coolies were collected and sent out to work. In addition to supplying the men, the Police officers in charge had in great many cases to arrange for their food and for their payment. The Police officers employed in the Casual Labour Department had frequently to work from 5,45 a.m. to 9 p.m. and sometimes later.

label: text
text: A special word of praise is due to the Police along the frontier of the New Territory, where owing to the outrageous behaviour of armed strike pickets, our constables and our police launches were frequently under fire and we were involved in a kind of guerilla warfare. The steadiness, self-control, courage and discretion of all ranks under these conditions were admirable. The gratitude of the Colony has been well earned by the Hongkong Police Force during the past ten months and it is a great pleasure to me to have this opportunity, on behalf of the whole community, of thanking you publicly.

label: text
text: MANAGING PARTNER IN TROUBLE.

label: text
text: A Chinese managing partner was charged at the Central Magistracy yesterday with making false statements to the Official Receiver relating to the affairs of the Wing Shing firm, of Koshing Street, and on other counts of falsifying the account books.

label: text
text:
Mr. E. S. C. Brooks prosecuted and Mr. L. R. Andrewes appeared for the defence.
Mr. M. W. Lo gave evidence of having prepared a sale agreement relating to the firm on the instructions of the accused. In reply to a question he said that he advised the accused to have the sale gazetted.
Other evidence was taken and the case was adorned until

label: text
text: Avising out of an incident at Causeway, Buy in which a Chinese was finally injured by a motor cycle," Mr. S. J. Squire was charged before Major C. Wilson at the Central Magistency yesterday afternoon with manalaughter, and also with driving a motor cycle in reckless manner.

label: text
text: Mr. J. A. Gordon Leask defended and Mr. H. S. Fitzroy watched proceedings on behalf of deceased relatives.

label: text
text: The first witness, a Chinese contable, said that he was on point duty at the junction at 9.15 p.m. on April 17 when he saw two motor cycles driven by Europeans with no pillion passengers travelling very fast towards the central district. The cycles touched each other in the middle of the road before passing the post and one of them turned into Caroline Road. The other ran over the man seated on the pavement and hit the tramway shelter. The driver of the machine fell on to the ground and was rendered unconscious. Witness also said there were two other Europeans on the scene shortly after the accident.

label: text
text: Dr. W. L. Paterson said the Chinese was admitted to the Government Civil Hospital and operated on immediately. Witness found the case hopeless and the man died two hours later. He thought the wound which proved fatal could have been caused by the front number plate of the motor cycle.

label: text
text: Witness said that Mr. Squire was also admitted. He had allight abrasions and was suffering from shock.

label: text
text: At this stage further hearing was adjourned until Friday afternoon.

label: paragraph_title
text: GIRL'S HAIR ABAZE

label: paragraph_title
text: PERIL OF ETHER PRODUCT USED BY A HAIRDRESSER.

label: text
text: 一

label: text
text: A warning to the public of the danger caused by hairdressers washing their women customers hair with etherol, an ether product, was given by a Paris court in a case which cost the life of a 17-years-old girl.

label: text
text: The victim, Mlle. Duprat, was having her hair washed with etherol when suddenly the hair caught fire. The hairdresser and his assistants wrapped blankets round her to smother the flames, but she died two days later after suffering great agony.

label: text
text: Her father was awarded £800 damages against the hairdresser, the court finding that the latter had failed to use proper precautions.

label: text
text: The saloon in which the girl's hair was being washed was separated from the rest of the establishment by a glass partition, but two panes were missing. Professor Kling, director of the Municipal Laboratory, found that the ether vapour had been ignited by heating apparatus in the adjoining room.

label: text
text: The court laid stress on the importance of making known profession: Kling's conclusion that the use of etherol was extremely dangerous in any circumstances the liquid being so volatile that the slightest air current might cause it to be ignited from a considerable distance.

text:
We have received for the Cathedral, from Mr. A. S. Abbott, a handsome altar service book, with markers for the different seasons. The old book was showing signs of much wear in this climate, so the gift is a most acceptable one.
The Choir.—We regret to have had many losses in the Choir, owing to departure from the Colony. Mrs. Mathieson, Mrs. Mather, Mrs. Morgain and Mrs. Gillham, have all left. We are glad to welcome Miss M. Stewart as a new member. And we should be glad to hear of several more ladies and gentlemen and boys to it! Up the ranks of the Choir. Surely those who have the gift of a good singing voice could use it for two hours a week to lead the worship of Almighty God.
We regret that the Rev. T. B. Powell is leaving on May 15, after a spell of service in Hongkong which has been all too short. He has done much good work during his brief stay here and his many friends will wish him every blessing in his future work wherever it may be.

label: text
text: The young Italian world eyellift has been joined in Hongkong by his companion, a young Czech Slovakian, named Antony Kundinger, who separated at Singn pore. Kundinger has had an adventurous trip through Cochin and Indo China. Like his companion he curries an autograph book which contains the signatures of well known people of 42 countries, with whom he has had interviews since he set out from Cape Town about five years ago.

label: text
text: The tourists hope to leave Hong Kong next week and make their way to Canton, proceeding to Peking later. They have even announced their intention of trying to cross the Behring Straits during the ice season! The homework route is to be by way of Japan and Canada.

MOSQUITO BREEDING ON MAINLAND
BOARD'S POWERS
It was mentioned in the course of debate yesterday at the Sanitary Board that the Board had no legal right to prosecute the owners of water areas beds whose methods of very cultivation led to mosquito breeding in the outlying district of New Kowloon. He proposed therefore that the necessity for resuming and draining such plots be pressed on the Government.
Dr. S. W. Tso said that admittedly Kowloon was developing in every way, but he felt that "these poor farmers should be protected." Their families had carried on the trade for hundreds

label: text
text: Dr. Koch said "apparently his colleague thought that the Sanitary Board were very hard on the farmers. The Board's intention was to carry out sanitation in the outside districts. The people's custom would not be interfered with, out the Board desired that the people should confirm to the ordinary rules of sanitation.

label: text
text:
Replying to Dr. Tso, the President said that it was a very difficult problem. The plots bred mosquitoes, and it was very desirable that the government should take control of them. And that the mosquito nuisance should be diminished.
Col. Boylan Smith seconded the resolution and it was carried unanimously.
Village Sanitation
On the proposition of the President, seconded by Mr. Wong Kwong tin, Dr. W. V. M. Koch, Dr. A. G. M. Severn, and Dr. S. W. Tso were appointed as a committee to carry out investigations with regard to village sanitation.
Those present were Mr. N. L. Smith (the President), Col. Boylan Smith, Dr. W. V. M. Koch, Dr. S. W. Tso, Mr. Wong Kwong tin, Dr. A. G. M. Severn, and Mr. R. A. D. Forrest (Secretary).
